comments.why: Moka pot coffee guide featuring James Hoffmann
comments.text: There's a great video with coffee expert James Hoffmann on making coffee in a moka pot: [VIDEO] However a moka pot generally doesn't make espresso as much as strong coffee. If you want something that makes espresso, check out the 9bar: [LINK] Of course you'll want a good hand grinder for either, but especially espresso. You can't get anything close to espresso with pre-ground or a cheap grinder.

comments.why: Tricks that improved the commenter's moka pot coffee
comments.text: I adopted a few tricks from either [1] or a similar video from James Hoffman’s Youtube channel some time ago (including the foaming milk with a French press one) and it vastly improved my lockdowns. The one useful thing they don’t say is (imo) it’s easier to get it right with a smaller size pot. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: ValentineC
comments.story: The Humble Brilliance of Italy's Moka Coffee Pot (2018)
comments.why: Start with hot water so grounds heat less
comments.text: James Hoffmann [1] and many others recommend starting with really hot water at the bottom, so the coffee grinds have less time to heat up. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: ValentineC
comments.text: James Hoffmann recommends using hot water in the moka pot: [VIDEO] I put mine (stainless steel) on my induction stove for 2, maybe 3 minutes maximum, and I've never encountered burnt coffee.

comments.author: masonhensley
comments.story: The Humble Brilliance of Italy’s Moka Coffee Pot (2018)
comments.why: Moka pot brewing tutorial alongside personal tips
comments.text: [VIDEO] I use one every day. Generally, fresh grounds, prewarm the water before assembly. I also like to wisk in a little sugar in the final cup after pouring out. (Don’t add sugar to the moka pot or it will caramelize/burn)
